## Napo River tours: an Amazon cruise or a stay in a lodge

The [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) flows through Ecuador's Amazon region and serves as a waterway to forest lodges, communities and protected natural areas. Unlike a short sightseeing boat ride on a lake, here boats are often the principal form of transportation: the road ends at a landing stage and the journey into the forest continues by water.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the Napo River on their main itineraries. Their essential difference lies in **where you stay and how deeply you experience the rainforest**. Options include a multi-day river cruise, an Amazon lodge stay and an extensive tour in which the Amazon occupies only one portion of an Ecuador and Galápagos journey.

## Which journeys follow the Napo?

| Program | Amazon format |
|---|---|
| [Mainland Ecuador in 9 Days](/ecuador/tour/luxury-mainland-ecuador-9-days/) | M/V Anaconda cruise |
| [Ecuador and Galápagos in 18 Days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) | Nature excursions at Sacha Lodge |
| [Best of Ecuador and the Amazon in 15 Days](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) | Forest trails and Sacha Lodge |
| [Andes and Amazon Wildlife](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/) | Napo River and Sacha Reserve |
| [Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/) | Canoe transfer to Casa del Suizo |

On the [9-day mainland Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/luxury-mainland-ecuador-9-days/), the Amazon portion starts with a flight from Quito to [Coca](/ecuador/place/coca/). From a landing stage on the Napo, guests travel by motorized canoe to M/V Anaconda before continuing aboard the vessel. The Amazon segment includes forest excursions, a community visit, wildlife observation and natural sites near [Yasuní](/ecuador/place/yasuni-national-park/) and [Limoncocha](/ecuador/place/limoncocha-biological-reserve/). After returning from the Amazon, the route continues into the Andes around Papallacta and Cotopaxi.

On the [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos trip](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the Napo is associated with a stay at Sacha Lodge. Activities include canoe transfers, views over the forest from high suspended walkways and trail walks. The [15-day Wildlife itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/) also visits Sacha Reserve: after the nature-focused Andean segment come rainforest trails, birdwatching and river crossings.

[Best of Ecuador and the Amazon in 15 Days](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) allows more time for mainland natural regions. Its river segment features Sacha Lodge, walking trails and a route above the forest canopy. On the relevant day, travelers may choose between a walk along the Napo and a more active Leoncillo forest trail; these are alternatives within one day, not two compulsory outings.

For set travel dates, consider the [11-day journey from September 1 to 11, 2027](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). After traveling from the Andes toward Tena, guests arrive in Punta Ahuano and transfer to a canoe. The ride downstream on the Napo to Casa del Suizo takes approximately 15 minutes. The Amazon segment is followed by Papallacta and the Galápagos Islands.

## Cruise versus lodge: the practical differences

A **river cruise** means living aboard a vessel while traveling between natural sites along the waterways. On M/V Anaconda, this combines observation from the deck, landings and evening and daytime outings. Compare the number of nights actually spent cruising and the excursions expressly listed, rather than relying solely on total tour duration.

An **Amazon lodge** serves as a fixed base for forest exploration. Guests leave for trails, crossings and observation points, then return to their accommodation. Sacha Lodge is associated with trails and a high suspension bridge, while Casa del Suizo offers a different set of forest and river activities. A facility described in the lodge's own advertising is not necessarily included in every Ada Tours itinerary.

| Criterion | Cruise / lodge |
|---|---|
| Overnight stays | On a vessel / at a forest lodge |
| Transportation | Ship and boats / local excursions |
| Program choice | Cruise route / lodge activities |
| Check carefully | Nights, meals, excursions |

## Preparing for the Amazon portion

The Napo region is hot and humid compared with high-altitude Quito. Rain is possible in different months, so pack light long-sleeved clothing, rain and insect protection, shoes with non-slip soles and a waterproof cover for documents and electronics. Trails may become slippery, and boarding small canoes requires care.

Pay special attention to **the timing between flights, road transfers and river crossings**. Depending on the itinerary, the Amazon portion starts near Coca or [Tena](/ecuador/place/tena/), in different parts of the Ecuadorian Amazon. Do not apply the crossing time for one lodge to another. When combining the Andes with lowland rainforest, allow for changing elevation and temperature over several days.

The Napo River is only one part of a vast natural region. Some programs include [Yasuní](/ecuador/place/yasuni-national-park/), [Sacha](/ecuador/place/sacha-reserve/) and other areas, but mentioning the "Amazon" or "Napo" alone does not guarantee a visit to every reserve. Specific trails, observation times and guiding conditions matter for wildlife encounters. Explore more of this theme in the [Ecuador wildlife tours catalog](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions about Napo River tours

### Is the Napo River a standalone excursion or part of the Amazon?

It is a major river and transport route in Ecuador's Amazon. On current itineraries, traveling along the Napo is usually linked to a lodge stay or a river cruise rather than one brief stop.

### Is a cruise included in every Napo tour?

No. The [9-day program](/ecuador/tour/luxury-mainland-ecuador-9-days/) uses M/V Anaconda; itineraries with Sacha Lodge and Casa del Suizo use canoes and lodge accommodation.

### Can I combine the Amazon and the Galápagos?

Yes. For example, the [18-day journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) and the [September 2027 itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/) include both natural regions.

### Are sightings of rare animals guaranteed?

No. Wild animals move freely in their habitats. Choose a program by confirmed trails, observation time and activities rather than a promise to see a particular species.

## North Plaza in the Galápagos: what lies beneath the water

North Plaza Island (Plaza Norte) lies east of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) in Ecuador. The two neighboring small islands, North Plaza and [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/), are often grouped on maps under the name Plazas. Their visitor opportunities differ, however. South Plaza has an authorized land visitor route, while North Plaza is closed to tourist landings and used for scientific research.

In our diving program, North Plaza appears as **one possible marine dive site**. That distinction matters: appearing on a list of dive sites does not grant permission to go ashore. The operator must confirm access to the actual underwater site and the route's compliance with National Park permits.

## Rocky slopes, sand and garden eels

The underwater terrain at North Plaza includes a rocky slope that gradually gives way to sandy seabed. This combination offers opportunities to observe different marine creatures during a dive. Reef fish gather around rocks; on sandy patches, divers may find garden eels, which emerge from their burrows and retreat quickly when approached.

White-tip reef sharks, rays and sea lions are possible encounters described for this site. Hammerheads and Galápagos sharks are mentioned in more open water. **These are potential wildlife sightings, not a list of guaranteed encounters.** Animal behavior, visibility and current direction vary even at the same site.

Underwater photographers may find both small seabed animals and larger creatures passing along the slope interesting. With garden eels, gentle fin movements are particularly important: approaching too quickly usually sends them into hiding.

## North Plaza and South Plaza: two different visits

It helps to distinguish the following options:

| Place | Main difference |
|---|---|
| North Plaza | Marine dive site; landing prohibited |
| [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) | Authorized walking route, iguanas, seabirds |

South Plaza is known for sea lion colonies, land and marine iguanas, prickly pear cacti and succulents that change color seasonally. It is an appealing nature walk, but visiting South Plaza **must not be represented as diving at North Plaza**. Even neighboring islands do not share interchangeable landing permissions or marine activities.

For watching coastal wildlife from land, choose a separately authorized landing itinerary; to look for garden eels and reef fish, a marine activity is necessary. Other known dive sites near Santa Cruz include [Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/) and [Mosquera](/ecuador/place/mosquera-islet/), each with its own conditions and experience requirements.

## How North Plaza may feature in a diving itinerary

On the [Ada Tours 4- or 5-day Galápagos Diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), accommodation is arranged on Santa Cruz. The short version has 2 diving days and the longer version 3, with 2 dives on each marine day. Specific sites are selected by the dive center according to the weekly schedule, weather, sea conditions and participants' experience.

The possible outings list includes a Plazas/Gordon grouping. **North Plaza appearing among the possible places does not promise a visit to that particular site.** Before booking, confirm which destination is permitted and planned for your date, and whether the dive center may change it if conditions deteriorate.

Participants need certification under a recognized diving system and must meet the dive center's requirements. If your experience is insufficient, discuss an alternative suitable site instead of choosing North Plaza based on its name. Arrange intervals between dives and before subsequent flights with the dive center.

## Visiting rules and responsible behavior

The Galápagos National Park regulates visits to terrestrial and marine sites separately. Visitors must use authorized operators and guides, stay within permitted zones and keep a safe distance from wildlife. Around underwater rocks, controlling buoyancy, avoiding contact with seabed organisms and not chasing sharks for photographs are particularly important.

When planning a trip to [Ecuador](/ecuador/), decide whether shore-based nature walks or scuba diving are your priority. Marine options appear under [diving journeys](/interests/diving/), and tours focused on island and marine wildlife under [Nature and Wildlife](/interests/wildlife/). Scenic walks on volcanic islands can be compared separately in the [Nature](/interests/nature/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about North Plaza

### Can tourists land on North Plaza?

No. North Plaza is closed to tourist landings; the open land visitor route is on neighboring South Plaza. Any marine activity near North Plaza must be confirmed separately.

### Are North Plaza and South Plaza one island?

No. They are two neighboring islands with different visiting regimes. They share the geographic name Plazas, but permits and types of excursion differ.

### Can hammerhead sightings be guaranteed?

No. They are among the potential open-water species, but sightings depend on natural conditions and the dive itinerary.

### Does every Galápagos diving tour include North Plaza?

No. On the [Ada Tours program](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), it is a possible site, not a mandatory stop. The decision depends on the schedule, permits and sea conditions.

### Is the site suitable for novice divers?

Eligibility depends on the exact site, currents, current conditions and the local dive center's assessment. Possessing a basic certificate does not in itself guarantee access to the chosen island.

## Adding a North Plaza dive to a Galápagos itinerary

[North Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/north-plaza-island/) lies near the eastern shore of Santa Cruz in the Galápagos. This catalog is about **a possible dive near the island**, not a landing. North Plaza is closed to ordinary tourist landings. Neighboring South Plaza is a separate island and a different excursion destination.

Our routes consider North Plaza as one of several potential dive sites. Its inclusion on a list does not mean the boat will necessarily come here: sites are selected according to schedules, sea conditions and National Park permits.

## Which program offers this possibility?

The [4- or 5-day Galápagos diving tour with accommodation at Hotel Fiesta](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) is based on Santa Cruz. The four-day version includes 2 days of diving, and the five-day version 3. **Each diving day includes 2 dives**. Between sea outings, travelers stay on the island and visit its highlands.

Potential destinations for a Sunday outing include Plazas / Gordon Rocks. These are alternative dive sites, not a sequence of stops guaranteed for all participants. A visit to Plazas must not be equated with walking on North or South Plaza. Confirm the actual marine site and activity before booking.

| Tour option | Diving |
|---|---|
| 4 days / 3 nights | 2 days with 2 dives each |
| 5 days / 4 nights | 3 days with 2 dives each |

Neither option inherently guarantees diving at North Plaza. If this is the primary goal of your journey, tell us when choosing dates and ask for confirmation of available dive sites.

## What can you see underwater?

At North Plaza, rocky underwater slopes give way to sandy areas. Garden eels, reef fish, white-tip reef sharks, rays and sea lions occur here. Larger pelagic animals, including sharks, may appear at outer sites. Wildlife changes with currents and seasons, so no particular species can be promised beforehand.

If your aim is to walk on land and observe birds and iguanas, consider [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) as a separate marine excursion option. If you want the rocky scenery and land iguanas of the Plazas, that means South, not North Plaza. For underwater activities, diving experience and conditions at the specific site remain decisive.

## What to confirm before booking

Ask about available sailing dates, the difficulty level of the proposed dive site, certification and experience requirements, medical restrictions, provided equipment and time before your return flight. The dive center selects the actual location with regard to safety, weather and accessibility.

Anyone wishing to be guaranteed a landing on an island should choose a different permitted site in the Galápagos. [Ecuador diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/ecuador/) allow travelers to compare suitable trip formats without confusing underwater activities with land-based sightseeing.

## Frequently asked questions about North Plaza diving

### Can I land on North Plaza during this tour?

No. Ordinary tourist landings on North Plaza are prohibited. This catalog describes a potential dive site off the island.

### Is a Sunday outing to Plazas guaranteed?

No. The weekly schedule lists possible dive sites. The decision depends on the actual outing, conditions and permits.

### Do both versions of the tour include North Plaza diving?

Both versions include diving days, but **North Plaza specifically is not fixed** for every departure. Check available sites before booking.

### How is North Plaza different from North Seymour?

This selection focuses on diving near North Plaza. [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) has an authorized walking trail for observing birds and sea lions, as well as separate marine dive sites.

## North Seymour Island: frigatebirds, boobies and nature walks in the Galápagos

North Seymour is a small uninhabited island of the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), north of [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). Travelers visit primarily to observe birds and reptiles. Dry palo santo trees, coastal rocks and wildlife habitats stand out in its open volcanic landscape.

This is a destination for observing animals in their natural environment. The itinerary centers on a walk and wildlife watching rather than beach leisure or strenuous trekking. Landings and walking routes are regulated by the National Park, and sightings of specific animals always depend on natural conditions.

## What wildlife might you encounter on North Seymour?

The island's best-known birds are **blue-footed boobies** and **frigatebirds**. Male frigatebirds display vivid red throat pouches during courtship. Boobies can be seen on land and near the water; their unusual blue feet are noticeable without approaching too closely. Swallow-tailed gulls and other seabirds also live here.

Land iguanas, marine iguanas and sea lions inhabit the island. North Seymour's land iguanas have an especially interesting history: according to Galápagos Conservancy, a group of iguanas was relocated here from Baltra during the first half of the 20th century. This illustrates how human intervention influenced the island's animal populations. Their presence is not an invitation to touch or feed them.

Galápagos wildlife may seem untroubled by people, but park regulations require **a distance of at least 2 m**, staying on marked trails and not disturbing birds. This allows visitors to observe colonies without interfering with their lives.

## How a visit to the island works

The trip generally involves a boat crossing, landing and a walk with an authorized naturalist guide. The walking route crosses open terrain, rocky and uneven in places. Athletic training is generally unnecessary for the standard walk, but comfortable shoes and sure footing on coastal rocks are helpful.

Waves and boat motion may be encountered during the crossing. There is little shade on the island, so bring a hat, water, sun protection and light clothing covering the skin. Use your camera without flash and maintain the required distance from nests and wildlife. Independent visits to protected areas without a licensed guide are not provided.

## Combining North Seymour and Bachas

North Seymour is a natural pairing with [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/) on the northern shore of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The first stop centers on watching birds on land, while the second offers a coastal lagoon, sandy shore and marine nature. Check which marine activities are included in the chosen program; weather may change the order and availability of landings.

Do not confuse this pairing with another popular itinerary: [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) is often combined with snorkeling near [Punta Carrión](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/). These are alternative excursion options, not four mandatory stops on one day.

## North Seymour in the Ada Tours itinerary

On our current [New Year tour, Entire Ecuador: Andes and Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), January 8, 2027, offers a choice of **one of 2 routes**. The first combines North Seymour and Bachas Beaches; the second visits South Plaza and Punta Carrión. The chosen option is confirmed after booking. For the first route, the itinerary specifies departure by yacht from the Itabaca Channel, a visit to the island, lunch on board and continuation toward Bachas.

North Seymour's appearance on the overall list of places therefore does not guarantee visiting the island. If birdwatching is a priority, ask which of the 2 routes has been confirmed. Explore other nature itineraries in our [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [nature travel](/interests/nature/) sections. For birds, iguanas and marine life, compare [wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about North Seymour

### What is the island famous for?

Frigatebird and blue-footed booby colonies, iguanas and an open volcanic landscape.

### Can I watch wildlife from very close range?

Animals sometimes approach the trail, but National Park regulations require visitors to stay at least 2 m away, including when taking photographs.

### Will every participant on the Ada Tours New Year journey visit North Seymour?

No. The tour offers 2 alternatives for that day. North Seymour and Bachas are visited only if that specific itinerary is confirmed.

## Which Galápagos tours may include North Seymour?

[North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) is known for blue-footed boobies, frigatebirds, dry volcanic coasts and sea lions. An authorized walking trail provides opportunities to observe nature. In this catalog, however, North Seymour is **a possible rather than guaranteed stop**: some tours choose either this island or South Plaza for their marine day.

When selecting a journey, determine whether the itinerary involves walking on the island followed by Bachas Beaches, an alternative excursion to South Plaza, or a separate dive near Seymour.

## North Seymour or South Plaza: how the marine day is chosen

On several of our itineraries, the Galápagos day follows one of two options:

- **North Seymour and Bachas Beaches.** Walk the island's authorized trail and observe birds and sea lions, then continue the marine program near Bachas.
- **South Plaza and Punta Carrión.** Visit another island with land iguanas and coastal landscapes, then explore the marine area around Punta Carrión.

These options are **alternatives**. They do not mean travelers visit both islands on the same day. The route is confirmed when organizing the trip. North Seymour is particularly interesting for birds and land-based observation, whereas South Plaza has different landscapes and a subsequent activity near Punta Carrión.

## Current programs to compare

On the [New Year journey, Entire Ecuador: Andes and Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), the island day after the mainland itinerary offers a choice between North Seymour–Bachas and South Plaza–Carrión. It suits those wishing to combine high-altitude Ecuador and the Galápagos.

On the [Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/), a similar alternative complements mainland attractions and a separate Pacific coast program.

The [Ecuador and Colombia: Galápagos, Andes and Caribbean Sea in 12 Days](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/) tour includes both countries and a marine excursion to one of the two islands during the Ecuador portion. For a longer itinerary, the [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) tour also features a Galápagos segment with alternative locations.

The standalone [Galápagos Diving: 4 or 5 Days](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) is about **underwater outings**. Its possible schedule mentions Seymour Channel and Seymour Northeast, which does not promise a walk on North Seymour. Distinguish scuba diving at sea from a land excursion along an island trail.

## When this choice is especially important

Birdwatchers should identify North Seymour as a priority in advance because frigatebird and blue-footed booby colonies are its leading natural attraction. Visitors interested in walking and photography likewise need a permitted landing: viewing the shore from a boat is not the same as walking the island.

The choice depends on vessel operations, available permits and the actual itinerary. Galápagos wildlife is protected, so approaching birds or sea lions for photographs is prohibited and the guide and park administration determine where visitors may walk.

Compare routes by their main geography in the [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/), and find more about the destination on the [North Seymour page](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/). At your request we can check which island and type of marine activity may be confirmed for your dates.

## Frequently asked questions about North Seymour tours

### Is North Seymour compulsory on every listed tour?

No. Some programs offer it as one of two alternative day routes. On diving tours, it is one of several possible marine areas, not a mandatory landing.

### Can I see North Seymour and South Plaza in one day?

The programs described here offer **one of two routes**, so you should not expect both landings in the same day.

### How does diving near Seymour differ from an island walk?

Diving takes place at marine sites and depends on underwater conditions. A land excursion follows an authorized trail and focuses on watching birds and sea lions.

### What should I check if frigatebirds are my main interest?

State North Seymour as a priority when selecting your trip and ask whether that landing can be confirmed. Even on a confirmed visit, sighting a particular animal is not guaranteed.
